info.name: AI Trading Platform API
info.description:
# AI Trading Platform – REST API

Backend of the AI trading analysis platform (FastAPI, PostgreSQL/TimescaleDB, Redis, Celery). This collection covers **every endpoint** (201 requests) with a saved example response for each request and its main error cases.

**Synced with backend commit `cc26716`** of `main`. The API contract is `docs/api/openapi.json` in the repository (WebSocket: `docs/api/asyncapi.yaml`). Swagger UI (`/docs`), ReDoc (`/redoc`) and `/openapi.json` are served locally, but **off in production** unless `API_DOCS_ENABLED=true`.

## Quick start

1. Import the collection and both files of `docs/postman/environments/`.
2. Pick an environment (**Production (VPS)** or **Local (Docker)**) and fill in `user_email` / `user_password` (and `admin_email` / `admin_password` for the Admin folder).
3. Send any request. Tokens are obtained, cached and refreshed automatically by the collection's pre-request script; you never paste a token by hand.

No account yet? Send **Auth → Register**: when `user_email` is empty, the new account becomes the collection's user.

## Authentication

| Method | How | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| Bearer JWT | `Authorization: Bearer {{access_token}}` (collection default) | apps, everything |
| Admin JWT | `Authorization: Bearer {{admin_access_token}}` (Admin folder) | `/admin/*` |
| API key | `X-API-Key: {{api_key}}` | external programs, read-only scopes |

Access tokens live 30 minutes, refresh tokens 14 days and are rotated on every refresh. Roles: `trader` (default on registration), `analyst`, `expert`, `admin`.

## Conventions

* Base path `/api/v1`; JSON in and out; all times are **UTC** (naive datetimes are taken as UTC).
* Chart data uses **unix seconds** in `time` (Lightweight Charts format).
* Lists are pages: `{"items": [...], "total": 123, "limit": 20, "offset": 0}`.
* Errors: `{"detail": "message"}`, or for validation (422) `{"detail": [{"loc": ["body", "field"], "msg": "...", "type": "..."}]}`.
* Someone else's resource answers **404**, never 403.
* Every response carries `X-Request-ID` (yours, if you send a sane one, else a new id): quote it when reporting a problem, it is on the server's log line for that request.
* An overloaded database answers **503** with `Retry-After` and `retry_after` in the body.

## Rate limits

Per identity (user, or each API key) per minute: trader 60, analyst/expert 300, admin 1,000. Indicator computation, strategy preview and backtest creation cost 5. Every limited response carries `RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining`, `RateLimit-Reset`; a 429 adds `Retry-After`.

## Running the whole collection

The folders are ordered so the **Collection Runner** can execute them top to bottom: each folder creates what it needs (workspaces, strategies, backtests, keys), uses it and deletes it again. Ids are passed between requests through environment variables (`instrument_id`, `workspace_id`, `backtest_id`, …). Every request has tests for its status code and documented fields.

> On **Production**, Register, Admin and the create requests write real data. Prefer the Local environment for full runs.

## Folders

Health · Auth · Users (me) · Market Data · Indicators · Strategies & Signals · Risk Management · Custom Strategies · Backtests · Workspaces · API Keys · News · Community · Price Alerts · Experts & Subscriptions · Chat · Expert Studio · Notifications · Admin · Realtime (WebSocket)

Maintained in the repository: `docs/postman/` (generated by `docs/postman/tools/`).

item.name: 02 · Auth
item.description:
Registration and JWT sessions.

* **Access token**: short lived (`expires_in` seconds, 30 min by default), sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
* **Refresh token**: 14 days, **rotated** on every refresh (the old one stops working).
* API keys are always refused here (403).

**Per-IP limits** on top of the normal rate limit: login 10/min (and 5/min per e-mail), register 5/min, refresh 30/min. 10 failed logins for one e-mail within 15 min lock that e-mail for 15 min.

> You rarely need to call Login yourself: the collection's pre-request script logs in with `user_email` / `user_password` and refreshes the token automatically.

item.description:
Instruments and OHLCV candles from TimescaleDB (1m hypertable + continuous aggregates for 5m, 15m, 1h, 4h, 1d).

* JWT, or an API key with the `market:read` scope.
* Candle `time` is the bucket start in **unix seconds (UTC)**: the format Lightweight Charts expects (`series.setData(candles)`).
* Naive datetimes in queries are taken as UTC.
* The **economic calendar** (`/calendar/*`) uses the same access.

item.name: Chart Image Analysis
item.description:
Upload a screenshot of a price chart and get a structured, checked analysis from Gemini (`docs/chart-analysis.md`): trend, patterns, support and resistance, indicators seen, an idea (buy, sell or wait, with a confidence) and a summary in Arabic or English. An educational aid, **not financial advice**: every result carries a fixed `disclaimer` added by the backend.

* JWT only, with a daily quota per role (UTC day): trader 5, analyst 20, expert 20, admin 100.
* The image is **never stored**, only its SHA-256, size, dimensions and type.
* Off until `GEMINI_API_KEY` is set: every request then answers 503 `not_configured` (the tests accept it).
* Errors are `detail = {code, message, …}` and never a 500.
* Recorded against `docs/postman/tools/fake_gemini.py`, a local stand-in for the Gemini API (no key, no paid call).

exec: try { json = pm.response.json(); } catch (e) { /* empty or non-JSON body */ }
// Save ids for the requests that follow
if (chart_analysis_id !== undefined && chart_analysis_id !== null) store.set("chart_analysis_id", String(chart_analysis_id));

request.description:
Multipart upload, answered synchronously (up to `CHART_VISION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, 45 s) with the stored analysis.

* `image`: PNG, JPEG or WebP (read from its bytes), at most 5 MB, at least 200 × 200 px.
* `language`: `ar` or `en` (default: your profile's language, else `ar`); `symbol` and `timeframe` are hints (the image wins).
* `result` (status `ok`): `is_chart`, `symbol_guess`, `timeframe_guess`, `trend`, `trend_strength`, `patterns`, `support_levels`, `resistance_levels`, `indicators_seen`, `idea` (`risk_reward` is computed by the backend, never the model's), `summary`, `reasoning`, `warnings`, `disclaimer`.
* The same image, language and hints within 24 h returns the stored result with `cached: true`: no new call and no quota.
* Each new call takes one unit of the daily quota; 422 `not_a_chart` is counted too. 429 `quota_exceeded` with `Retry-After` (seconds to 00:00 UTC); 503 `busy`, `model_busy`, `model_unavailable` or `timeout` with `Retry-After` (no quota taken).

**Auth:** Bearer JWT (`{{access_token}}`) · **Rate-limit cost:** 5 · **Success:** `200`, `503`

item.description:
Posts, comments, likes, follows, public profiles and reports (`docs/news-posts.md`). JWT only.

- Analysts, experts and admins publish posts (traders get 403, and the runner skips to **Follow user**); everyone can read, comment and like.
- `visibility`: `public`, `followers`, or `subscribers` (experts only): readers without the expert's `premium_posts` perk get a teaser (`locked: true`, the first 200 characters, no attachments, comments hidden and closed).
- Bodies are **Markdown stored as written**: render them with raw HTML disabled. Raw HTML and `javascript:` links are refused (422).
- Comments have two levels: a reply to a reply is stored under the top-level comment.
- Followers get `new_post`, authors `comment_reply` and a batched `post_liked` notification; nobody is notified about their own actions.

Daily limits: 10 posts per 24 h, 60 comments per hour, 20 reports per day (429 with `Retry-After`).

The experts directory and buying a subscription (`docs/subscriptions.md`). **Payments are demo only: no real money.** The flow still works like a real provider: a hosted checkout page, a signed webhook, renewals, failed payments, cancellation, refunds and invoices.

A subscription unlocks the perks of its plan: `premium_posts` (posts with visibility `subscribers`; others get a teaser with `locked: true`), `chat` (the **Chat** folder) and `signals_feed`. | `4000 0000 0000 0002` | declined at checkout |
| `4000 0000 0000 9995` | succeeds now, renewals fail |

item.description:
One conversation per expert and subscriber (`docs/chat.md`). REST for sending and history; live delivery on the WebSocket topic `chat:<conversation id>` (`chat_message`, `chat_message_updated`, `chat_read`, `chat_typing`; see the **Realtime** folder).

- A subscriber with the `chat` perk opens the conversation and writes; the expert can always reply. When the subscription ends the conversation is read-only for the subscriber.
- Either side can block; only the side that blocked unblocks. Admins read every conversation but do not write.
- The recipient gets a `chat_message` notification only while none of their connections is subscribed to the conversation (at most one external notification per conversation per 5 minutes).

Limits: 30 messages per minute, 2,000 per day (429).

item.name: 18 · Notifications
item.description:
The notification inbox, per-event / per-channel preferences, the Telegram link and push devices (`docs/notifications.md`). JWT only: API keys get 403.

| `type` | Produced by |
|---|---|
| `signal` | live signal engine, for your activations with `notify: true` (carries your trade plan) |
| `backtest_completed` / `backtest_failed` | backtest worker |
| `security` | sign-in from a new IP / device, password changed, API key created or revoked, account locked |
| `system` | admin broadcast, test messages |
| `new_post` / `comment_reply` | someone you follow published / a comment on your post or a reply to yours |
| `post_liked` | "N people liked your post": one row per post and day, **in-app only** |
| `content_hidden` | moderation hid your post or comment |
| `price_alert` | one of your price alerts fired |
| `chat_message` | a chat message while you are not looking at the conversation (one external notification per conversation per 5 min) |
| `subscription_started` / `_renewed` / `_payment_failed` / `_canceled` | your subscription to an expert |
| `new_subscriber` | someone subscribed to your plan (experts) |
| `ai_setup` | an AI setup became ARMED on an instrument you follow, or one you took changed state (carries your size) |

Every event is stored in the inbox and pushed on the WebSocket as `notification`. Telegram, email and push follow your preferences: event on for the channel → signal filters → quiet hours → hourly cap (held deliveries go out later as one digest). A channel the server has no settings for reports `enabled_on_server: false` and its deliveries are `skipped`.

By the time the Collection Runner gets here, the inbox already holds real events from the folders before (password changed, API key created / revoked, backtest completed).

The Telegram webhook (`POST /telegram/webhook/{secret}`) is called by Telegram itself, only in `TELEGRAM_MODE=webhook` behind HTTPS, and is not a client endpoint: the server uses long polling for now.
